Predicted Means and Pairwise Comparisons as Data Frames

Source: R/tidy.R
tidy.predictmeans.Rd

Return the means or pairs table of a predictmeans result (glance(): one row describing it). The tables have fixed column names (see the Value section of predictmeans) and unrounded values, which makes them easy to use in further analysis, reports, Shiny apps or AI tools. tidy() is the generic from package generics (also used by broom); as.data.frame() needs no other package. coef() and vcov() return the means (on the model scale, as in the estimate column) and their covariance matrix (Kenward-Roger adjusted when the means are), named by the mean labels. With them, multcomp::glht() or marginaleffects::hypotheses() can test any contrast of the means, e.g. hypotheses(pm, hypothesis = "n2 - n0 = 0") (normal-based). Recent versions of marginaleffects need the class listed first: options(marginaleffects_model_classes = "predictmeans").

Usage

# S3 method for class 'predictmeans'
tidy(x, what = c("means", "pairs"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'predictmeans'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'predictmeans'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE,
              what = c("means", "pairs"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'predictmeans'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'predictmeans'
vcov(object, ...)

Arguments

x

A result of predictmeans.

object

A result of predictmeans.

what

Which table: "means" (the default) or "pairs".

row.names

Optional row names for the result.

optional

Not used.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame; for coef() a named vector and for vcov() a matrix. glance() gives one row: modelterm, n.means, n.pairs, nobs (observations in the cells), df.method, adjust, level, vcov, vcov.adjust, sed.min, sed.mean, sed.max (standard errors of the differences), lsd.mean, nperm and model.class.

See also

predictmeans, autoplot.predictmeans, advice

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
  Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
  fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)
  pm <- predictmeans(fm, "nitro:Variety", atvar = "Variety", adj = "tukey")
  as.data.frame(pm)
#>    nitro     Variety  estimate std.error       df  conf.low conf.high

  head(as.data.frame(pm, what = "pairs"))
#>            level1          level2          by  estimate std.error       df
#> 1   0:Golden Rain 0.2:Golden Rain Golden Rain -18.50000  7.682948 45.00014

#> 6 0.4:Golden Rain 0.6:Golden Rain Golden Rain -10.16667  7.682948 45.00014
#>   statistic      p.value        p.adj  conf.low   conf.high      lsd
#> 1 -2.407930 2.020357e-02 9.004248e-02 -33.97425  -3.0257499 15.47425

#>   adj.conf.low adj.conf.high p.method
#> 1    -38.99579      1.995794    tukey

  if (requireNamespace("generics", quietly = TRUE)) generics::glance(pm)
#>       modelterm n.means n.pairs nobs     df.method adjust level  vcov
#> 1 nitro:Variety      12      66   72 Kenward-Roger  tukey  0.05 model
#>   vcov.adjust  sed.min sed.mean sed.max lsd.mean nperm model.class
#> 1        TRUE 7.682948 9.160819 9.71502 18.64525    NA     lmerMod

  # Any contrast of the means from coef() and vcov(): Victory - Golden Rain at nitro 0.6
  b <- coef(pm)
  L <- (names(b) == "0.6:Victory") - (names(b) == "0.6:Golden Rain")
  c(estimate = sum(L*b), SE = sqrt(drop(L %*% vcov(pm) %*% L)))
#>  estimate        SE 
#> -6.333333  9.715020
